questions.question: How can I run components built with Wasm Shell?
questions.answer: You can use wash to create and publish WebAssembly components for any runtime or runtime environment that supports the WebAssembly Component Model, including wasmCloud, Spin, jco, wasmtime, and others.

questions.question: What are the differences between Wasm Shell (wash v2.x and higher) and wasmCloud Shell (wash v1.x and below)?
questions.answer:
wasmCloud Shell, the previous iteration of wash, was designed as a utility for building WebAssembly components and managing deployments for wasmCloud 1.x and below.

Wasm Shell (wash v2.x and higher) is a more tightly focused utility for WebAssembly component development, designed to be usable across the Wasm ecosystem.

This means that many commands and features that were available in wash v0.x are not included in Wasm Shell. For example, Wasm Shell does not create capability providers, manage wasmCloud deployments, or include the Washboard UI; it adds wash update for self-updates, pushes and pulls components with wash oci push and wash oci pull, and runs a wasmCloud host with wash host instead of wash up.

questions.question: How do I set up a TinyGo project for wash build?
questions.answer:
TinyGo projects use a Makefile to wrap the build steps and a .wash/config.yaml file to tell wash which commands to run.

Your .wash/config.yaml should specify the build command, for example "make bindgen build" for build and "make build" for dev. Your Makefile invokes TinyGo directly with the -wit-package and -wit-world flags, for example: tinygo build -target wasip2 -wit-package ./wit -wit-world hello -o my-component.wasm ./

For full instructions, see the Go Language Guide.
